headline: High-risk default interaction: Cursor can read/write shared workspace files and use MCP/network, while aci can emit CRM/email/calendar actions that Cursor may treat as trusted input.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can surface content through MCP/function calls and broad network egress, while Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if aci writes attacker-controlled text into files or messages Cursor later parses as commands. The pathway is not provably blocked in either profile.
conditions: IF aci writes untrusted text into a shared file, note, or message that Cursor later opens
IF Cursor parses file or clipboard content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of shared files into Cursor agent runs
Keep aci outputs in a separate, non-workspace channel
Require manual review before Cursor acts on aci-generated text
Use provenance tags or prefixes for all aci outputs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress; Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, and clipboard contents and can call model providers and MCP servers. If sensitive aci-derived data lands in the shared workspace or clipboard, Cursor can transmit it onward to third parties by default. The pair therefore creates a realistic exfiltration path.
conditions: IF aci outputs CRM/email/support data into files or clipboard-visible text
IF Cursor sends those files or buffers to model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep sensitive aci outputs out of the shared workspace
Disable clipboard-based transfer for sensitive material
Restrict Cursor model-provider access for sensitive projects
Use separate OS accounts or workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before any upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write to mutable resources: aci can call APIs such as Google Sheets, Notion, email, CRM, and Cursor can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shell commands. Cursor also supports multiple instances with shared state via local filesystem, so concurrent edits from aci-triggered artifacts and Cursor actions can collide and overwrite work. This is a default-capability conflict.
conditions: IF aci and Cursor target the same document, repo, or CRM record
IF Cursor runs in Yolo mode or otherwise auto-runs edits while aci is also updating shared state
mitigations: Assign separate ownership for files and records
Pause one agent before the other writes shared state
Use branch-per-agent workflows for git
Lock shared documents during agent runs
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks across tools

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and research outputs, while Cursor can act on files, shell, git, and MCP results. If Cursor treats aci-produced text as authoritative, it may commit, send, or deploy incorrect actions without verification. The pair has a clear downstream action-taking chain, and the blast radius can be irreversible.
conditions: IF Cursor uses aci-generated text as the basis for code, commits, or external messages
IF no human or automated verification step checks aci outputs before Cursor acts
mitigations: Require a verification step before any Cursor action based on aci output
Mark aci outputs as untrusted until reviewed
Disable auto-run for Cursor on aci-derived tasks
Use diff-based review before commits or sends
requires-engineering: add policy gates for action execution

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, customer support, and calendar data, while Cursor touches open files, clipboard contents, and sends data to model providers. If regulated or customer data from aci is placed into Cursor workspaces, retention and residency obligations can diverge because the profiles show different vendor stacks and no shared compliance controls. The mismatch is plausible but not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from aci is copied into Cursor-managed files or prompts
IF the deployment requires residency, retention, or deletion guarantees not documented for both agents
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Cursor prompts or files
Use synthetic or redacted data for development
Review vendor retention settings before use
Separate compliance-sensitive workflows from general coding
requires-engineering: document and enforce a shared data-handling policy
